newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan-little effect from foreign bond holdings.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan-little effect from foreign bond holdings.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday said there was little effect on short-term rates from foreign purchases of U.S. treasury bonds.
In testimony before a House Banking subcommittee, Greenspan also took the view that tightness in the oil service industry was unlikely to increase energy prices and thus inflation.

"I'm aware that there is difficulty in getting (oil drilling) equipment, but I'm not aware that there is a significant concern that crude availability will be foreshortened in a manner that will induce significant acceleration of prices."

Turning to the issue of the impact of foreign holdings of U.S. treasuries, Greenspan said "the best way to describe it is you probably have some small effect in the short run when very large changes in purchases occur (but) there is no evidence that over the long run that interest rates are materially affected."

Greenspan also dismissed the idea put forward by one questioner that there was any agreement between the United States and foreign central banks to buy U.S. treasury paper. "There is no such agreement," he said.
